identity.name: Nautilus Travel Time Chronograph
identity.one_liner: Dual-time-zone flyback chronograph in the Nautilus case, with local and home time on jumping hour hands.

comps.condition: 2019, full set, certificate of origin, presentation box

provenance_events.description: Patek adds the Travel Time complication to the Nautilus chrono case — a dual time display with day/night indicators at 3 and 9, flyback chronograph, on the CH 28-520 C FUS caliber. The 5990/1A becomes the most-asked steel Nautilus of the late 2010s.
A 2019 5990/1A-001 with certificate and full set sells at the Phillips Geneva Sessions Spring 2024 online auction for CHF 88,900 (with premium), inside the high estimate.

Patek releases the 5990/1A — the Travel Time Chronograph version of the 5980, with a dual-time display and a flyback chronograph. The 5990/1A becomes the most-cited Asian Patek chronograph of the 2010s, with a multi-year waitlist at Hong Kong ADs.

narrative.story: Introduced in 2014, the 5990/1A packed Patek's Travel Time module — skeletonized home-time hand, day/night windows, pushers in the left case flank — onto the flyback chronograph base of the 5980. It is the busiest steel Nautilus dial and the most functional one. The blue-dial 5990/1A-011 refresh arrived in late 2022 alongside the 5811.
narrative.collector_notes: The four case-flank pushers make polishing history easy to spot; check the analog date sub-register at 12 tracks local time after any service. The -001 and -011 dials are different markets.
